name: Stephen J. Scott

events.title: Widow in 1860 census
events.description: Julia A. 'Scot', 50, domestic, b. Penna, with Ann, 15 - Stephen not in household, consistent with his death in 1856.

bioAdditions:
No record of Stephen's own parentage was found, but three new pieces of evidence bear on it. (1) The FamilySearch tree names his parents as Daniel Scott and Hannah Devens (no sources attached to the link) (S2). Hannah Devens, daughter of Leendert (Leonard) Devens, was baptized at the Walpack Dutch Reformed Church, Sussex Co., New Jersey, in 1787 (FamilySearch index, S3). A Leonard Devens of Plymouth Twp left a will registered in 1839 (Luzerne Will Book B p.20) (S4), and Elizabeth Devens, 'wife of Leonard', died 30 Jan 1858 aged 80 and was buried in the Shupp Cemetery at Larksville, Plymouth Twp (S5). So a Devens family was in Plymouth Twp in Stephen's lifetime, which makes the Devens link worth testing. (2) In 1810 a 'Daniel Scott Jr.' headed a household in Pittston Twp, Luzerne Co.: one man aged 26-44, one woman 16-25 and three children under 10, two of them boys (S6). That fits a couple with a son born in 1806 and a wife born about 1787, though it does not name anyone. (3) Against a Pennsylvania birth, his daughter Catherine told the 1910 census that both her parents were born in Connecticut (S7), as Bradsby said in 1893; the 1850 census says Pennsylvania. The Connecticut statement could reflect the family's Connecticut (Susquehanna Company) background rather than Stephen's own birthplace.

Julia Ann was a widow in July 1860, living in Plymouth Twp with her youngest daughter Ann (S1). No will or estate entry for Stephen appears in the Luzerne wills index (S4).

openQuestionsNew: Read Leonard Devens's will (Plymouth Twp, registered 1839, Luzerne Will Book B p.20): does it name a daughter Hannah Scott (or Covert) or grandson Stephen Scott?
FamilySearch's Hannah Devens has a Find a Grave index entry as 'Hannah Devens Covert' - did Daniel Scott die c.1811 and Hannah remarry a Covert?
Search Luzerne Orphans' Court for guardianship of Daniel Scott's minor children c.1811-1820.
